sources.locator: Ch. 1 §1(b), Propositions 1.28 and 1.37, printed pp. 17-18 (PDF 28-29); Ch. 3 §3(g), Lemmas 3.19-3.22, Theorem 3.23 (Cartier) and Corollary 3.24, printed pp. 69-72 (PDF 80-83); Ch. 10 §10(a)-(e), Definitions 10.1/10.5/10.6/10.11, 10.14-10.23 and Propositions 10.28-10.29, printed pp. 186-196 (PDF 197-207). Read in full over these ranges.

contents.name: Ch. 1 §1(b), Proposition 1.28 (smooth = regular at e = geometrically reduced) and Proposition 1.37 (dim Tgt_e(G) <= dim G, equality iff smooth)
contents.reason: These propositions supply the dimension-theoretic input of Milne's own proof of Cartier's theorem, recorded as the independent alternative treatment; the local proof uses the free-differentials route instead.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(g), Lemma 3.19 (smooth iff dim Tgt_e(G) = dim Tgt_e(G_red))
contents.reason: Step of Milne's alternative Oort-style proof of Theorem 3.23, recorded as the independent treatment; not consumed by the local free-differentials proof.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(g), Lemma 3.20 (if every nilpotent of O(G) lies in m_e^2 then G is smooth)
contents.reason: Step of Milne's alternative Oort-style proof of Theorem 3.23, recorded as the independent treatment; not consumed by the local free-differentials proof.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(g), Lemma 3.21 (x lies in W iff x tensor y lies in W tensor V' for y nonzero)
contents.reason: Linear-algebra step of Milne's alternative Oort-style proof of Theorem 3.23, recorded as the independent treatment; not consumed locally.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(g), Lemma 3.22 (A = k + I and Delta(a) = a tensor 1 + 1 tensor a mod I tensor I for the augmentation ideal I)
contents.reason: Hopf-algebra input of Milne's alternative Oort-style proof of Theorem 3.23, recorded as the independent treatment; the local proof instead uses the freeness of the differentials.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(g), Theorem 3.23 (Cartier: every affine algebraic group over a field of characteristic zero is smooth)
contents.reason: Independent complete treatment of the same theorem, read in full and recorded as the alternative route in the item sources; the local proof follows Stacks 39.8.2 and its calculus of free differentials.

contents.name: Ch. 3 §3(g), Corollary 3.24 (in characteristic zero all finite algebraic groups are etale)
contents.reason: Not consumed by this pair: the scaffold claims smoothness of affine groups in characteristic zero, and no etaleness statement for finite group schemes is promised or used by any item here.

contents.name: Ch. 10 §10(a), Definition 10.1 (Lie algebra over a field: bilinear bracket, alternation, Jacobi) and Example 10.3 (associative algebras and gl_n as Lie algebras)
Ch. 10 §10(b), Definition 10.5 (adjoint map ad(x) and the derivation law) and 10.14 (Lie is a functor)
contents.reason: The adjoint map and the functoriality of Lie are absorbed into the bracket theorem, which defines [X,Y] = ad(X)Y and proves functoriality; 10.14 is also used by the tangent-space lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 10 §10(b), 10.6 and display (56): L(G) = ker(G(k[epsilon]) -> G(k)) = Hom_k(I_G/I_G^2, k)
Ch. 10 §10(b), 10.7 and display (57): L(GLn) = {I + A epsilon} and the bracket as the commutator of lifts
Ch. 10 §10(b), 10.8-10.10: Lie algebras of U_n, of a vector group V_a and of the subgroup fixing a tensor
contents.reason: The unipotent and tensor-fixing computations are not consumed by any item of this pair; the vector-group case 10.9 is instead absorbed by the B-page example ex-lie-algebras-of-alpha-p-mu-p-and-gl-n.

contents.name: Ch. 10 §10(b), 10.11: the correspondence X <-> e^{epsilon X}, with e^{epsilon(X+X')} = e^{epsilon X} e^{epsilon X'}
Ch. 10 §10(c), 10.15-10.17 (faithfulness of Lie on smooth connected subgroups of a connected group)
contents.reason: No faithfulness statement for smooth connected groups is promised or used by this pair; only the following remark that Lie(alpha_p) = Lie(G_a) is harvested, and it is recorded on the B-page entry.

contents.name: Ch. 10 §10(d), 10.18-10.21 and display (61): g(R) = g tensor R, the adjoint action x e^{epsilon X} x^{-1} = e^{epsilon Ad(x)X}, and its naturality
Ch. 10 §10(d), 10.22-10.23: ad = Lie(Ad), the bracket [x,y] = ad(x)y, uniqueness of the functor Lie, and the GLn commutator
Ch. 10 §10(e), Proposition 10.28 (L(G) = Der_{k,epsilon}(O(G),k)) and Proposition 10.29 (left-invariant derivations with the commutator bracket)
contents.reason: The scaffold's definition route is the cotangent and dual-number one; the equivalent description of the Lie algebra by left-invariant derivations with the commutator bracket is not consumed by any promised item of this pair.

contents.name: Ch. 10 §10(f)-(h), 10.30-10.35: stabilizers, centres and centralizers of algebraic groups and Lie algebras
contents.reason: Stabilizer, centre and centralizer computations are not part of the promised inventory of this pair and are left to the later group-action and reductive-group pairs.

contents.name: §3.6-3.9, 3.9.0 and 3.9.0.2: the tangent functor T_{X/S}(M) and Lie(X/S,M) = ker(T -> X) as a group functor
§3.7 with footnote (50), §3.10 and §3.11: functoriality of the tangent and Lie functors, monomorphisms and the derived morphism L(f)
Definition 4.1.A, Proposition 4.1.1 and Remarque 4.1.C: the adjoint operation Ad(x)X = i^{-1}(s(x)i(X)s(x)^{-1}) and its naturality in the group and in M
§4.2-4.3 and Remarque 4.3.3-4.3.5: derived morphisms, the case of O_S-modules, and d: F -> Lie(F/S)
contents.reason: The scaffold uses the functor-of-points form of the adjoint representation and does not need the relative derived-morphism calculus for O_S-module functors, which is not consumed by any item of this pair.

contents.name: §4.4-4.5, Definition 4.6, Lemme 4.6.2 and Theoreme 4.7: good S-groups, representable groups are good, and Lie(Aut(F)/S) = End(F) with id + tX
contents.reason: The identification of the tangent space with End(F) via id + tX is exactly the GL_n computation, restricted to our affine group over a field; the surrounding good-group formalism is not separately scaffolded.

contents.name: Definition 4.7.2 (bracket [x,y] = ad(x)y) and 4.7.3 with note (79): the bracket as the commutator of independent lifts, functoriality in G, and skew-symmetry
Proposition 4.8: Ad(g)Y = g o Y o g^{-1} and [X,Y] = X o Y - Y o X for the automorphism group of a module
Corollaires 4.8.1-4.8.2 and Scholie 4.9: the Jacobi identity, the representation law rho'([x,y]) = [rho'(x),rho'(y)], and the summary of the bracket axioms

contents.name: Lemma 39.6.3 [047I]: Omega_{G/S} = f^*C_{S/G} = f^*e^*Omega_{G/S}, free over O_G when S is the spectrum of a field

contents.reason: The local proof of Cartier's theorem in this batch uses only the freeness of the differentials and the characteristic-zero smoothness criterion; the equidimensionality statement is not consumed by any item here.

contents.name: Lemma 39.8.2 [047N] (Cartier's theorem: a locally algebraic group scheme over a field of characteristic 0 is smooth)
contents.reason: Independent complete treatment of the theorem; the local proof follows the same route through Lemma 39.6.3 and the characteristic-zero smoothness criterion, restricted to the affine case.

contents.name: Remark 39.8.3 [047O] (group schemes over a field of characteristic 0 are reduced, citing Perrin) and Lemma 39.8.4 [047P] (reduced locally algebraic groups over a perfect field are smooth)
contents.reason: Neither the external reducedness reference nor the positive-characteristic reduced case is consumed by this pair; reducedness in characteristic zero follows here as a consequence of smoothness and regularity, not as an input.

contents.name: Lemma 10.140.4 [00TU]: for a Noetherian local ring containing k with residue field finitely generated and separable over k, the map m/m^2 -> Omega_{R/k} tensor kappa is injective
Lemma 10.140.5 [00TV]: for a finite-type k-algebra with kappa(q) separable over k, smoothness at q, regularity of the local ring and freeness of the differentials at q are equivalent
contents.reason: The local scaffold replaces the smooth-iff-regular equivalence by the Jacobian local-chart theorem and proves only the direction free implies regular, so this lemma is recorded for comparison and is not consumed by any item.

contents.name: Lemma 10.140.6 [00TW]: if Omega_{S/R} = S df + C then f is not nilpotent, and if S is Noetherian local then f is a nonzerodivisor
Lemma 10.140.7 [00TX]: over a field of characteristic zero, at a prime, smoothness, freeness of the differentials and regularity of the local ring are equivalent
Lemma 10.140.3 [00TT]: smoothness at q, the bound dim Omega tensor kappa(q) <= dim_x X and its equality form, with regularity of the local ring
contents.reason: This dimension-count criterion is not consumed by the local proof, which goes from free differentials to regularity by the induction of Lemma 10.140.7 and then to smoothness by the Jacobian criterion.
